question: In which of the following organisms can individuals change sex, indicating that sex is NOT genetically determined?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Snails**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Many species of **snails** exhibit the ability to change sex, a phenomenon known as **sequential hermaphroditism**.
 
• In these species, individuals can function as both males and females at different times in their life cycle.
 
• This ability to change sex is **not genetically predetermined** but is instead influenced by environmental and social factors.
 
• The process of sex change in snails can be triggered by factors such as the **availability of mates** and the **presence of certain chemicals** in their environment.
 
• This adaptation can enhance the reproductive success of snails in varying environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lizards**__

 __
 
• **Most lizard species** have sex determined genetically, not environmentally.
 
• Some lizards, such as the **New Mexico whiptail**, reproduce through parthenogenesis, but do not change sex.
 
 
 
• **Frogs**__
 __
 
• Although some frog species can change sex, this is relatively rare and typically a response to specific environmental conditions.
 
• This phenomenon is observed in species like the **Common reed frog**.
 
 
 
• **Ostriches**__
 
 
• **Ostriches** are birds with genetically determined sex and do not exhibit sex-changing behavior.
 
• They are known for their large size and flightless nature, native to **Africa**.
